text: Why is photonic true-time-delay (TTD) required for wideband phased-array beamforming above roughly 10% fractional bandwidth?
choices: Electronic phase shifters implement a frequency-independent delay, which causes beam squint
Photonic TTD digitizes the RF signal faster than any electronic ADC
Electronic phase shifters cannot drive more than two antenna elements
Electronic phase shifters impose a frequency-dependent delay (beam squint) for wideband signals, whereas photonic TTD gives a true frequency-independent delay
explanation: A fixed phase shift corresponds to a delay that varies with frequency, so different frequencies steer to different angles (squint) over wide bandwidths; photonic TTD (e.g. dispersive fiber) provides a genuine frequency-independent time delay, the only viable approach above ~10% fractional bandwidth at mm-wave. Option 0 swaps the property (phase shifters are NOT frequency-independent), and TTD is a delay element, not an ADC or an element-count limitation.
